kurz: Which political influences show up measurably in prices, which cannot be demonstrated statistically, and why your own convictions distort your view of both.

bloecke.md:
On 9 September 2026, a barrel of Brent crude cost $109.51. Four trading days later it cost $130.80, a rise of 19.4%. The increase was triggered by the escalation surrounding Iran. Here a political event moved a price directly and demonstrably, which rarely happens.

The market values cash flows and the interest rate at which they are discounted. Opinions do not enter into this valuation. Politics therefore only has an effect to the extent that it changes cash flows or the interest rate. On this basis, three channels can be distinguished. The first is measurable, the second cannot be demonstrated in the statistics, and the third lies in the investor's perception rather than in the market.

bloecke.titel: Oil prices before and after the escalation, September 2026
bloecke.unter: Brent rose by 19.4% in four trading days, the US grade WTI by only 10.0%. The unusually large price gap of around $24 shows that the shock hit the volumes traded by sea rather than supply within the US.

bloecke.md:
A chain of effects that has nothing to do with sentiment leads from the oil price to your portfolio. The German inflation rate rose from 2.3% in June to 2.8% in July and 2.9% in August 2026. Energy became 10.5% more expensive, motor fuels 27.7%. The core rate excluding energy and food remained at 2.4%. The price pressure therefore came from outside, not from the domestic economy. Such a development is called a [[supply shock]]. It raises prices and at the same time lowers real demand, which is why every central bank has to choose between two objectives in such a situation.

In September 2026, the ECB and the Fed decided to act against inflation expectations. On 10 September, the ECB raised all three key interest rates by 25 basis points. The deposit facility rate has stood at 2.50% since 16 September. The Fed followed suit on 16 September and raised its target range to 3.75% to 4.00% with effect from 17 September. The yield on ten-year Bunds reached 3.58% on 15 and 16 September, its highest level since April 2011. Via the commodity price, inflation and the discount rate, politics thus reached the price of every share and every bond. Party manifestos played no part along this route.

Political events almost always reach prices via an intermediate stage such as a commodity price, a tax, a regulation or the key interest rate. If no such intermediate stage can be identified, there is usually no effect on prices either, and the event remains a headline.

## Elections, governments and returns

The most obvious question is the hardest to answer, namely whether the country is governed better under one party than under the other. For the US from 1949 to 2012, Alan Blinder and Mark Watson measured a growth advantage of around 1.8 percentage points a year under Democratic presidents. According to their own analysis, however, the gap is mainly due to oil prices, bursts of productivity and foreign demand, that is, to circumstances that no president determined.

The main statistical problem is the small sample. Blinder and Watson analysed sixteen terms of office. Since the launch of the DAX in 1988, Germany has had five federal chancellors. Nothing can be said about causality from five observations, and hardly more from sixteen. The same problem exists with the inverted yield curve. It has anticipated every US recession since 1955, but the sample comprises only around a dozen cases. With so few cases, chance hits can look like fixed laws.

The error only becomes expensive through the action that follows from it, namely when an investor sits out an unloved legislative term in an instant-access savings account.

bloecke.titel: The cost of sitting it out (illustrative calculation)
bloecke.unter: Calculated for €100,000 over 30 years at 7% in the stock market and 2% in an instant-access savings account, excluding taxes and costs. Four years out of the market cost 17% of final wealth, eight years almost a third.

serien.name: Final wealth in thousands of euros

bloecke.md:
Invested throughout: 1.07^30 = 7.612, so €761,200.

Eight years out of the market: 22 years at 7% give a factor of 4.430, eight years in an instant-access savings account at 2% a factor of 1.172. Together this gives a factor of 5.191, so €519,100.

That is 31.8% less final wealth for 26.7% less time in the market. Each year in an instant-access savings account instead of the stock market multiplies final wealth by the factor 1.02 / 1.07, that is, reduces it by around 4.7%, and these reductions compound. With fixed returns, the loss therefore depends only on the number of years out of the market and on the return gap, regardless of when those years fall. If an investor also gets out at an unfavourable moment, they lose even more. Election nights are rarely market lows.

## Regulation

Regulation is the political intervention that a market can price in, because it names a sector, a date and an amount. A standard example is the German nuclear phase-out. The acceleration of the phase-out in 2011 under Section 7(1a) AtG (Atomic Energy Act) set the remaining operating lives by law, and on 15 April 2023 the last three reactors were disconnected from the grid. On 6 December 2016 (1 BvR 2821/11), the Federal Constitutional Court (BVerfG) ruled that the phase-out was essentially permissible. However, it required compensation for investments that had lost their value and for residual electricity volumes that could no longer be generated. The operators subsequently received around €2.4 billion. The ruling thus protected the operators' property, but not the continued existence of their business model.

Interventions do not have to be this fundamental to have an effect. From December 2022 to June 2023, the Electricity Price Brake Act (Strompreisbremsengesetz) skimmed off surplus revenues of certain electricity generators. The rent brake (Mietpreisbremse) under Sections 556d et seq. BGB (Civil Code) has been extended until the end of 2029 and thus limits the income side of every residential portfolio in designated areas. The EU fleet regulation 2019/631, as amended in 2023, sets the target value for new cars from 2035 at zero grams of CO2 per kilometre. Today, every valuation of an automotive supplier discounts back from this date.

bloecke.titel: Checking the regulatory risk of a sector position
bloecke.md:
- What counts first is what share of revenue depends on the regulated business. At 10%, an intervention is a nuisance, at 70% the whole investment depends on it.
- It matters whether the price or the quantity is regulated. Price caps reduce the margin immediately, quantity requirements take effect over years.
- Also consider the lead time and any grandfathering. A ban from 2035 has a different effect from a levy starting next quarter.
- It also needs to be clarified whether the intervention can be challenged in court. A duty to pay compensation and legal proceedings can halve its effect and delay it by years.
- Only a rule that has already been published in a law gazette or official journal provides a reliable date. An announcement in an interview is not enough for this.

Tax law is a form of regulation that affects every German portfolio, regardless of sector. Under Section 32d EStG (Income Tax Act), capital income is subject to flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) of 25% plus solidarity surcharge, 26.375% in total. The saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) is €1,000, or €2,000 for joint assessment, under Section 20(9) EStG. Equity funds have a 30% partial exemption (Teilfreistellung) under Section 20 InvStG (Investment Tax Act), and accumulating funds are taxed on an ongoing basis through the advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale) under Section 18 InvStG.

Each of these figures is the result of a political decision, and they change. Until 2008, price gains were tax-free after a holding period of one year. The 2008 business tax reform (Unternehmensteuerreform 2008) abolished this with effect from 1 January 2009 and only [[grandfathering|grandfathered]] existing holdings. From 1 January 2021, loss offsetting for derivative transactions (Termingeschäfte) in Section 20(6) EStG was capped at €20,000 a year. At the end of 2019, a limit of €10,000 had been adopted, and the Annual Tax Act 2020 (Jahressteuergesetz 2020) raised it even before it came into force. The Annual Tax Act 2024 removed the restriction again. So within these four years there were two U-turns, and whether some strategies paid off depended on nothing more than one sentence in the Income Tax Act.

If the entire advantage of a structure comes from a tax rule, the risk lies in the legislative process rather than in the market. This risk can be neither diversified nor hedged. Tax advantages are fine as a side effect of an investment, but they are of little use as the main reason for it.

## Price movements in wars and crises

The idea that wars trigger long bear markets does not stand up to the data. Even among the largest daily losses of the DAX, the triggers are mixed.

bloecke.titel: The five largest daily losses of the DAX and their triggers

bloecke.md: Two of the five days with the heaviest losses had a political or military trigger, three did not. More important than the individual day is the [[recovery time]], that is, the time from the old peak until this peak is reached again. The decline of the S&P 500 in 1990 began at the high of 16 July, 17 days before the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait on 2 August, and cost 19.9% by the low on 11 October. It had been recovered by 13 February 1991, 212 calendar days after the high and while the war was still going on.

bloecke.titel: Recovery time of the S&P 500 after selected declines
bloecke.unter: The two declines with the clearest external trigger (Gulf War 1990 and coronavirus 2020) were recovered fastest. Recovery took a long time where valuations and the credit system were the cause.

bloecke.md: The depth of a decline says little about its duration. The coronavirus decline cost 33.9% and had been recovered after just under six months. The shallower rate shock of 2022 cost 25.4% and took just over 24 months. The severity of the event does not explain this difference. It depends on whether the same profits are discounted at the same interest rates afterwards. A war shifts supply chains, whereas a valuation bubble or a disrupted credit channel shifts the cash flows themselves.

## Distortion through your own convictions

The third channel is the distortion of your own perception, and it is the only one that is certain to have an effect. In September 2026, it could be read from the data. According to preliminary figures, the University of Michigan's consumer sentiment index stood at 47.8 points, and the German consumer climate indicator at −26.6. Such values are otherwise familiar from severe recessions. The hard data, that is, counted transactions, showed a different picture.

US retail sales vs previous month (Aug)
US initial jobless claims (week ending 12 Sep)
Euro area GDP vs previous quarter (Q2)

bloecke.md:
A survey measures an assessment, and assessments are coloured by party politics. People who reject the government in office regularly rate the economic situation more gloomily. After a change of government, these assessments reverse within weeks, even though nothing has changed in the facts. At the checkout, by contrast, how you voted plays no role. Initial claims for unemployment benefit and retail sales are counted events, and political convictions do not change them.

This does not mean that you should ignore sentiment data. They are available early and are useful for turning points. It does mean, however, that you need to check your own reading of them. Investors who think a government is bad almost automatically consider its economic policy harmful. They find confirmation of this in the data, because surveys supply this confirmation.

bloecke.md: This results in a ranking of influences. For the return over the next ten years, the valuation level is probably more important than any election result. The Shiller P/E of the S&P 500 stood at 40.94 on 18 September 2026, while the historical average is 17.42. The Buffett indicator stood at 244% of GDP at the end of June 2026. These figures are independent of who governs, and they appear in no election manifesto.

Election dates are fixed long in advance, manifestos are public, and polls run for months. By election night, the most likely outcome is therefore priced in, and the price only reacts to the deviation from it. The same mechanism works with economic data. There too, prices react to the deviation from expectations and not to the published value. That is why the rare cases in which elections moved markets strongly were almost always surprises. By definition, surprises cannot be traded in advance.

mitnehmen: Politics reaches prices via intermediate stages such as commodity prices, taxes, regulations and the key interest rate, and where none can be identified, it usually remains a headline.
The question of which party is better cannot be answered statistically, because sixteen US presidential terms and five German chancellorships are too small a sample.
In the model, eight out of thirty years out of the market cost just under a third of final wealth (€519,000 instead of €761,000).

In the examples shown, declines with a clear external trigger, such as the Gulf War in 1990 or coronavirus in 2020, were recovered fastest, while recovery took a long time after valuation and credit crises.
Surveys measure assessments and are therefore coloured by party politics, counted transactions are not.

begriffe.text: A disruption on the supply side, such as a jump in the oil price, that raises prices and dampens real demand. It confronts central banks with a conflict of objectives, because fighting inflation puts additional strain on the economy.

The risk that laws or regulations change the earnings of a sector, through price caps, quantity requirements, levies or bans. If a position is heavily concentrated in the regulated business, this risk cannot be eliminated through diversification.
The time from a peak until the same peak is reached again. It is only loosely related to the depth of the decline and depends more on whether the cause shifts profits and interest rates permanently.

A rule under which a change in the law leaves existing situations unaffected. In tax law, this applies, for example, to securities bought before 1 January 2009, which therefore remained exempt from flat-rate withholding tax on price gains.
